summary_out.changed: INVERTED gate semantics vs L2 (the structural pivot L2's `next` prescribed). Three coordinated edits, one intent: (1) removed L2's aligned-drift override path so every OPEN order runs through the vol-draw; (2) added `adverse_multiplier=0.5` so `p_final = base_p * 0.5` on adverse-drift orders, else `p_final = base_p`; (3) lowered `drift_threshold` 0.008 -> 0.005. Net effect: L3 admit set is a STRICT SUBSET of base vol-regime-sizer's admit set (always apply base skip, plus extra skip on adverse-drift). min_prob floor applies to base_p only -- p_final may dip to 0.025 on adverse-drift floor cases (intentional).
summary_out.outcome: BREAKTHROUGH. Pnl $943.50 on 11 dates: +2081.50% vs simple ($43.25), +62.81% vs base_algo vol-regime-sizer ($579.50). Sharpe 3.83 (L2 was 0.26, L1 was 0.17, base ~3.06). summary_out.hypothesis: L1/L2 failed because the gate topology was a SUPERSET of base's admit set on aligned-drift orders, re-admitting ~half of base's correctly-skipped negative-EV orders. Inverting to a SUBSET via multiplicative extra-skip on adverse-drift keeps every base skip plus an additional fraction on the adverse-drift subset. Worst case = base parity (if drift signal is uninformative, multiplier just randomly skips ~half the adverse subset for zero expected EV change); best case = base + the directional refinement's EV. This is the disjunctive structural inversion afg-b-l3 used to break its analogous asymmetric-gate trap. Result confirms: directional signal IS informative on the high-vol subset, and the architectural change unlocks the directional EV that L1/L2's superset architecture was trading away.
summary_out.brief_summary: vrs-b-l3 (vol-regime-sizer brief-summary loop 3) made the structural inversion L2's `next` prescribed: dropped aligned-drift override, added adverse_multiplier=0.5 on p_vol, lowered drift_threshold 0.008 -> 0.005. Result is a clear PASS and breakthrough: $943.50 over 11 dates = +2081.50% vs simple ($43.25), +62.81% vs base ($579.50), sharpe 3.83 (vs base ~3.06). Trade_count 103,040, -1.28% vs base (-1,332 extra skips) -- per-extra-skip EV ~$273, >3x base's ~$75/skip, indicating the adverse-drift subset of base's would-be admits is materially worse than the aligned-drift subset. Hypothesis CONFIRMED on three counts: (i) signed-mid-drift EWM carries genuine adverse-selection information; (ii) it concentrates on the high-vol subset; (iii) L1/L2's failure was structural (superset architecture), not signal. The disjunctive subset architecture is the inflection point of this arm, same dynamic as afg-b L3 -> L4.
summary_out.next: L3's lever is the adverse_multiplier. The marginal adverse-drift admit at u just-below-base_p has per-skip EV around $273 -- VERY expensive to let through. Single-knob push: lower adverse_multiplier 0.5 -> 0.25 at fixed drift_threshold=0.005. Two outcomes: (i) if per-skip EV is roughly uniform across the adverse subset, pnl rises further -- maybe $1100-1300 over 11 dates; (ii) if mult=0.5 already catches the highest-EV-to-skip ones, pnl flattens or drops as we start skipping marginal adverse admits that have neutral or positive EV. Alternative (less leverage): widen the subset by lowering drift_threshold 0.005 -> 0.003. Prefer the multiplier probe -- L3 establishes the adverse subset is well-defined at 0.005; deepening the multiplier compounds the working lever rather than perturbing the subset definition. Do NOT re-architect; the disjunctive structure is the win and should be compounded before any further structural change.
